title: Leaderboard vs Collaborative Challenge
panelPrompt: Click a format to see who it suits and what it risks.

image.style: flat vector comparison poster, clean figure and scoreboard icons, muted textbook palette
image.overall: A three-column comparison poster about competition formats in a coding club, arranged left to right from highest risk to safest. Each column is a tall rounded panel with a coloured header bar carrying its printed title, and simple flat icons below. The three printed headers, and the ONLY text in the image, are: "Leaderboard" (left), "Friendly Competition" (centre), "Collaborative Challenge" (right).
image.layoutNotes: Divide the content area into 3 equal-width vertical columns with a clear gutter of background between each pair. Every column must have the SAME width, top edge, and bottom edge so the overlay's hover zones line up exactly. Each column has its printed header in bold dark text at the very top, on a tinted header bar in that column's accent colour, with simple flat icons below. No other text anywhere. Leave at least 4% margin at the left and right edges and 8% at top and bottom. The left column's header bar is red, the centre's amber, and the right's green, so the poster reads as a risk gradient from left to right. Do not draw any names, scores, digits, or rankings inside the scoreboard icon -- use blank rows only.

zones.label: Leaderboard
facts: Ranks every student by a running total
Strugglers see the same low rank week after week
Highest risk of discouraging the students who need encouragement most
Best reserved for confident, evenly-matched groups

draw.position: The left column, roughly 2% to 32% of the image width.
draw.visual: Header bar tinted red. Below it: a tall scoreboard panel with blank ranked rows (no names or numbers), a single figure at the top with a small crown, and a smaller figure at the bottom drawn slumped.

zones.label: Friendly Competition
facts: Scored by team, not by individual name
Re-pairs teams between rounds so no student stays 'on the losing team' all session
Framed with humour rather than stakes
Gives a quick energy boost without a lasting scoreboard

draw.position: The centre column, roughly 35% to 65% of the image width.
draw.visual: Header bar tinted amber. Below it: two small groups of two figures facing each other, a stopwatch, and a pair of circular arrows suggesting teams being re-paired between rounds.

zones.label: Collaborative Challenge
zones.summary: One shared goal, no ranking at all.
facts: Requires combining multiple students' skills into one outcome
No student can finish it alone
Builds group identity instead of rivalry
Safest choice for a mixed-confidence group

draw.position: The right column, roughly 68% to 98% of the image width.
draw.visual: Header bar tinted green. Below it: four figures arranged in a ring around one shared object, and several differently-shaped puzzle pieces interlocking into a single completed shape.

quiz.question: Which format carries the highest risk of discouraging strugglers?
Which format is the safest choice for a mixed-confidence group?
Which format re-pairs teams between rounds?
